sections.title: Pros
sections.narration: Pros first: tomatoes bring a distinctive lycopene story. That antioxidant identity is a more tomato-specific strength than generic low-calorie praise. High water content gives a lot of food volume for few calories. Tomatoes are useful for adding bulk and freshness without much calorie cost. Works raw or cooked in a lot of meals. That versatility is one reason tomatoes are easy to use regularly rather than just admire nutritionally.

sections.title: Cons
sections.narration: The drawbacks next: it contributes freshness more than serious energy or protein. A tomato can improve a meal, but it usually does not do the heavy lifting by itself. Acidity can be rough for some people. Tomatoes can aggravate reflux or sensitivity in a way that is specific enough to mention. Flavor and quality swing a lot with ripeness and season. That does not erase the nutrition case, but it does affect real-world usefulness and appeal.
